sections.summary: Manage your own FILMUNITY identity and professional profile, separately from association administration.

articles.title: Understand your representative account
articles.why: Your login identifies you as an individual and gives you authorized administration of your registered association. These are separate responsibilities.
before: Who: the verified account owner; representatives may read profile help while their registration is pending.
Use your own authorized login; complete required email verification.
steps: Open Dashboard to review your profile summary and FILMUNITY membership details.
Open Professional profile to complete your professional information and passport photo.
Use Association Management for organization settings; use Members Management for applicants and members; use Financial Management for association books.
Representatives with a pending or approved registration cannot use personal association-membership application, payment or renewal workflows. This does not remove your FILMUNITY identity.
articles.result: You can distinguish personal identity from the association records you administer.
avoid: Do not share the representative password with another officer. Delegated finance roles are not yet implemented.
Representative access does not automatically create a paid membership of the association.

articles.title: Build and publish your professional profile
articles.why: A complete profile helps members recognize the association representative.
before: Who: the verified account owner; representatives may read profile help while their registration is pending.
Prepare a clear portrait/passport photo, work bio, portfolio details and public contact links.
Publish profile requires name, username, industry, role, profile photo and work bio. Every retained portfolio project needs title and credited role.
steps: Choose Professional profile, then Edit profile or the relevant section Edit control.
Complete the profile wizard and save each required step. Upload your passport photo for digital cards.
Review professional details, industry/role, images, bio, social links and portfolio.
When the profile meets the publication requirements, choose Publish profile. After later edits choose Publish updates.
Use View public profile or Copy link to check and share the published page.
articles.result: Your public professional page reflects the version you deliberately published.
avoid: Do not put association bank credentials or private applicant documents into your public profile.
Public profile sharing QR and membership-validity verification QR serve different purposes.

Unpublish removes public availability without deleting your private draft. Public-profile links and media are public only after publication; avoid private contact/evidence unless deliberately intended for public viewing.

articles.title: Maintain account identity and security
articles.why: Login settings are private account data, separate from the published professional profile and association branding.
before: Who: signed-in account owner. Start: account menu → Settings → Profile, Security or Appearance. Some sensitive actions require password confirmation.
Use your own account; keep current access to the verified email and recovery methods.
steps: In Profile review Name and Email address, then Save. Changing email can require verification again before verified-only workflows are available. Use the verification resend link when offered.
In Security enter Current password, New password and Confirm password, then Save. Use the password rules shown by the current installation; never share the values in a help request.

Use the offered two-factor/passkey controls only with your own authenticator/device; complete confirmation and retain recovery codes privately. Their visibility depends on configured authentication features.

Appearance changes your account's display preference. It does not change association Brand accent or frozen document branding. Use the separate professional-profile Publish updates action to publish professional changes.
articles.result: Account settings do not approve an association, activate membership, change financial permissions or rewrite posted records.
articles.example: Meena Example uses meena@example.test in synthetic tests. Passwords, passkey secrets and recovery codes are deliberately not included.
avoid: Account deletion is destructive: read its confirmation separately; this guide is not an instruction to delete the account.
Google sign-in requires configured provider support. Never enter credentials into an association payment/proof form.

articles.title: First-day setup checklist
articles.why: Consistent setup prevents wrong fees, duplicate member numbers and confusing communications.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant. Start: Association dashboard → Workspace setup.
Association registration must be approved; collect logo, official mailbox, authorized fees and the last issued membership number.
steps: Open Association dashboard and confirm the organization name.
Open Workspace setup. Configure official contact email, display name, description, accent and logo.
Configure mandatory Yearly and Life-Time fees, plus any additional named plans.
Configure the next membership number, prefix and padding using the numbering guide.
Create required membership fields and acknowledgement descriptions; preview the form.
Write clear payment instructions, then Save workspace settings and verify the saved result.
Initialize finance only after agreeing the cutover date and receipt classifications with the responsible accountant/officer.
articles.result: Applicants see your configured form and approved applicants can confirm the intended plan and fee.
avoid: Do not ask applicants to send passwords, card PINs or OTPs.
Do not keep an unsaved setup form open while another officer changes settings; reload after a version conflict.

articles.title: Configure membership plans and fees
articles.why: Applicants choose a plan after approval; confirmed fees must remain stable for that application.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant. Start: Association dashboard → Workspace setup.
Have the association-approved fee schedule.
steps: Set required Yearly and Life-Time fees in Workspace setup.
Use Add membership plan for optional names such as Student or Associate. Choose a Yearly (12 months) or Life-Time term, enter the INR fee and availability.
Save settings. Review the plan list shown to an approved applicant.
Uncheck availability to archive a custom plan. Once used, its term cannot be changed; create a different plan instead.
Before archiving a yearly plan, decide how existing members will renew: an inactive plan cannot be newly selected or renewed in this release.
articles.result: New confirmations use the current configured fee; existing confirmed applications, payment requests and receipts keep their agreed snapshots.
articles.example: Associate Yearly costs ₹1,000. If you later change it to ₹1,200, an already-confirmed ₹1,000 application stays ₹1,000. A later confirmation uses ₹1,200.
avoid: Changing a plan fee is not a way to adjust an existing payment request.

articles.title: Continue your existing membership numbers
articles.why: You can carry forward an existing series without renumbering previous members.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant. Start: Association dashboard → Workspace setup.
Verify the last actually issued number and identify its prefix and numeric portion.
steps: Open the membership numbering controls in Workspace setup.
For last number SISA-6000325, use prefix SISA-, next number 6000326, and padding appropriate to your agreed format.
For a purely numeric series beginning at 1000, use an empty prefix, next number 1000, and no extra padding.
Save and verify the displayed configuration before activating the next real membership.
Keep a written cutover record. Legacy membership import preview can review existing source numbers without creating members or advancing this sequence; there is no import write action yet.
articles.result: New activations continue the configured sequence; existing numbers stay unchanged.
avoid: Enter the next number to issue, not the last number already issued.
Receipt numbering is separate from membership numbering.
Do not move a series backwards or activate dummy real members to experiment with numbers.

articles.title: Understand platform review and audit views
articles.why: FILMUNITY platform review permissions are separate from association ownership. Owners cannot grant themselves platform-wide access.
before: Who: configured FILMUNITY reviewer/auditor only for the named views. Start: FILMUNITY Admin, Registered accounts, Association review or Payment audit when those navigation items are offered.

Use Payment audit to inspect payment requests, submission evidence and receipts within the authorized audit scope. These screens do not provide arbitrary member/ledger editing.
Return to association-specific workflows for operational decisions. Do not repeat activation, modify posted history or share an audit download to resolve a mail-delivery issue.

articles.example: A fictional pending Demo Film Association can be approved by an independently configured reviewer; that reviewer cannot approve their own registration.
avoid: Never infer permission from a visible copied URL; the server enforces access again.

articles.title: Review an application
articles.why: Approval of the application comes before plan confirmation and payment verification.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant managing this association; member self-service is described separately.
Confirm you are in the correct association; have your review criteria available.
steps: Open Membership applications. Use Pending review, search or sortable columns to locate the applicant.
Expand the row to read submitted answers and download evidence. Review decision notes and application references.

Choose Review to inspect the application. Use Approve → Confirm approval when requirements are met, or Decline, enter Reason for declining and Confirm decline. Approval displays Approved but internally means accepted_for_payment, not activated membership.
After acceptance, ask the applicant to select and confirm a membership plan and fee in their own account.
Do not activate membership merely because the application has been accepted. Continue with Application Payments.
articles.result: Accepted applicants can confirm their plan; declined applicants see a decision note.
avoid: Do not approve solely because a document file is present; verify its content and source.
Association representatives are not eligible to start another association membership under the configured representative policy.

articles.title: Request payment and verify proof
articles.why: A proof upload is a claim of payment; the association must verify receipt before activation.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant managing this association; member self-service is described separately.
Application accepted, applicant plan/fee confirmed, and payment instructions configured in Workspace setup.
steps: Open the accepted application and verify that the applicant used Confirm plan and fee. Use Request payment, review Payment instructions and Due date (optional), then Send payment request. The confirmed amount and plan are frozen.
The member opens My payments, enters Transaction reference, Payment date and Payment proof, then Submit for verification.
Open the payment and Download proof. Independently compare amount, date, destination and reference with bank/cash evidence.
Choose Return proof with Reason for returning for incorrect evidence, or Acknowledge payment → Confirm once funds are verified.

Acknowledgement activates membership, allocates its native membership number, issues the membership receipt and exposes its card/workspace. Confirm zero-fee membership → Confirm uses the explicit zero-fee path without bank proof.
Check View receipt and the membership status/term. Retry email delivery retries failed communication without repeating activation.
articles.result: The member receives an active membership and receipt after the association confirms payment.
articles.example: A screenshot says ₹5,000 was transferred. You cannot find that transfer in the association bank record. Return/request clarification rather than acknowledge the screenshot.
avoid: Application Payments is the operational member-payment workflow; Financial Management is the association accounting ledger.
Clicking a finance reversal does not reverse a bank transfer or cancel membership.

articles.title: Review expiring memberships and send a reminder
articles.why: The admin renewal queue focuses on yearly memberships near expiry under the 30-day policy.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant managing this association; member self-service is described separately.

Search and expand the member row. Check expiry and existing renewal/payment history.

Use Send reminder email → Confirm send where offered. Reminder sent today disables another same-day send; Retry reminder email is offered for a retryable failed attempt. Delivery state and retry limits remain visible.
The eligible member confirms their renewal fee and submits payment evidence through their own account.
Verify and acknowledge the renewal payment using the same care as the initial payment.
Check the resulting term and receipt: early renewal extends from current expiry; after expiry the new term starts at acknowledgement.

articles.title: Legacy membership migration: read-only import preview
articles.why: Legacy membership migration: read-only import preview. Use the current association-scoped screens.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant only. Start: Members → Legacy membership import preview.
Have an XLS, XLSX or UTF-8 CSV export and verify that member numbers were preserved as text. No legacy import write action exists.
steps: Select Association and the file. Set Worksheet (zero-based), Header row (1–20) and CSV delimiter, then Read columns. The current file is parsed from temporary request storage and is not retained.
Under Column mapping map the eight supported fields in order. Exact FILMUNITY template headers map automatically; manual overrides remain available. Choose Source timezone explicitly.

Choose Validate mapped rows (no import). Review Source SHA-256, Source sample and Preview results: Ready for later import review, Existing matches, Needs correction and Manual identity review. Each flagged row shows Source row and reasons; use Previous/Next for 50-row pages.
Correct the source file or mapping and preview again. Ready means only that preview validation passed. No memberships, accounts, financial balances or numbering sequences are changed.
articles.result: Duplicate numbers in the file, existing same-association matches and ambiguous identities are separated without exposing other associations' private members.
articles.example: Text member number 000123 and Tamil name மீனா உதாரணம் remain unchanged. A Yearly row starting 2026-04-01 requires an end after that date; a Life-Time row must have no end date.
avoid: Never repair lost leading zeros by guessing. Ambiguous numeric/scientific identifiers need source correction; formula cells are rejected, not executed.
Phone and address are source context because the current member account has no native phone/address fields. Status and source IDs are not accepted import columns.
This preview never merges users, marks them verified, renews an expired membership or reserves a new member number.

sections.summary: Start with setup, then enter, review and post documents, allocate settlements, reconcile bank and TDS, and export. articles.title: Start here: the financial workflow
articles.why: Set up the books, record and review documents, settle outstanding bills, reconcile money and TDS, then export a reviewed batch. Posting and matching are separate actions.
before: Who: the signed-in applicant of an approved association registration, managing that association. There is no separate delegated finance approver role in this release.
Start: Financial Management → Finance overview. Have an accountant-reviewed cutover date, opening balances and ledger classifications. Examples below are synthetic inputs, not statutory tax advice.
steps: Open Settings and initialize the books on the verified Books start date. Create needed Accounts, member and vendor ledgers; enter balanced opening vouchers only on that cutover date. Opening balances are not bill-wise opening invoices and are excluded from Tally XML.

For member charges use Invoices and settlements → New invoice · F8. For tax-aware invoices or vendor bills use GST / TDS billing → New tax-aware invoice / bill after saving reviewed tax configuration. Save creates a draft only.

Inspect Details, Double-entry lines and any tax snapshots. Use Submit for review, then Review and post, enter Decision note, check I confirm this decision., and Confirm. Only posting changes the ledger; membership activation is a separate membership payment workflow.

Record a New receipt against the member ledger or New payment against the vendor ledger. Review and post, then Apply settlement / credit against the original posted invoice/bill. An unallocated receipt or payment remains available as an advance.

Use Details → Settlement allocation history, Outstanding / available and Party ledger to verify results. Compare bank statement lines in Ledger and Save clearance. Match TDS challans only after a separate posted TDS remittance; matching creates no accounting entry.

Correct posted history using linked credit/debit notes or a reviewed reversal; release allocations and challan matches when required. Print the stored document. Review Reports and exports, including excluded records and mappings in TallyPrime XML export, before closing a period.
articles.result: The ledger records posted movements, bill tracking records active allocations, bank clearance records statement matches, and challan reconciliation records how a posted TDS payment is assigned. These balances answer different questions.
articles.example: Member Meena Example: post invoice ₹5,000.00, post a ₹2,000.00 receipt, allocate the full ₹2,000.00 to that invoice. Invoices and settlements → Outstanding / available is ₹3,000.00; Details → Settlement allocation history shows ₹2,000.00. Party ledger shows debit ₹5,000.00 and credit ₹2,000.00 (₹3,000.00 net debit, assuming no other entries). Vendor Stagecraft Example: pre-GST ₹1,000.00 + illustrative 18% GST ₹180.00 = gross ₹1,180.00; reviewed TDS ₹100.00 leaves party payable ₹1,080.00. A separately posted ₹100.00 TDS remittance can be recorded and matched to that bill; matching does not reduce the vendor payable.
avoid: Never enter an invoice receipt a second time as a generic donation or membership receipt.
Example rates, thresholds, legal references and certificate decisions require your own accountant's review. The app does not choose statutory applicability.

Legacy membership migration remains preview-only. Invoice reminders have no live delivery or reminder schedule. Accounts reported a successful TallyPrime 7.2 import with no errors; per-ledger reconciliation and repeat-import behavior remain pending unless separately evidenced.

articles.title: Monthly recurring member invoice drafts
articles.why: Monthly recurring member invoice drafts. Retain the stored source records and review results before proceeding.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant for this association.
Start: Invoices and settlements → Recurring member invoices. Create the member receivable and eligible income/fund/liability classification ledgers first.
steps: Complete Create template in the order below, using Add line or Remove line as needed. Save template stores future generation settings; it does not post or collect money.
Choose Generate due drafts for due active templates. Next scheduled date, recent generated draft links and generation/pause activity show the result. Each generated draft snapshots template values.

Use Edit future values to change name, due days or lines for future generation only. Member and original monthly schedule stay fixed. Pause disables generation; Resume (skip past periods) discards scheduled dates before today, while a date due today remains eligible.

Open each generated draft and use the normal explicit Submit for review and Review and post workflow if appropriate. Repeated manual/scheduled runs cannot create a second invoice for the same template and billing month.

For operators: filmunity:generate-recurring-invoices reuses the generator across associations. Laravel registers it daily at 01:00 in the app timezone (current config UTC), with overlap protection. This repository registration does not enable an operating-system/production scheduler.
articles.result: Invoices remain drafts. One template/period is enforced transactionally by database uniqueness. Active catch-up is limited to 24 periods per template/run; failures are audited and retryable without duplicating completed drafts.
articles.example: A template starting January 31 generates February's last day and then March 31, without drifting to March 28/29. Due after calendar days 10 means billing date plus 10 days. Changing a ₹5,000.00 line to ₹5,500.00 leaves earlier generated snapshots at ₹5,000.00.
avoid: No automatic posting, payment collection or reminder delivery is included.
Closed periods or unavailable ledgers stop work for that template; scheduled processing records generated/skipped/failed outcomes and continues other templates. Inspect activity before retry.
Paused missed periods are not backfilled on resume; active missed periods can be caught up.

steps: Read Current eligible invoice preview: Invoice, Recipient, Due date, Outstanding · INR and Qualification. All posted outstanding invoices can qualify, including those not yet due. Drafts, fully settled and reversed invoices are excluded.

Queue reminder (live send disabled) creates/reuses a daily occurrence for the invoice and normalized recipient in the app timezone. The worker rechecks status, current balance and recipient before attempting delivery.

Use Refresh queue status to see queued, sending, sent, skipped, failed or uncertain outcomes and Queue attempt audit history. Sent in this release means a test mail fake, not an external email; live delivery is guarded off.

For confirmed non-delivery use Retry same occurrence. A completed job does not send again. Operator tests may exercise the billing-reminders database queue using a fake mailer in filmunity_test. Do not enable live sending or configure reminder scheduling from this guide.

articles.example: After the member example allocation, the preview shows ₹3,000.00 outstanding. Paying and allocating that remaining amount before the worker runs makes the invoice ineligible; the queued occurrence must not mail a stale ₹3,000.00 balance.
avoid: These invoice reminders differ from existing membership-renewal reminders, whose configured notification workflow can send email.

Start: Finance → Reports → TallyPrime XML export. Have posted basic accounting vouchers and independently verified ledger mappings in a separate TallyPrime 7.2 test company. Do not import into live books.
steps: Select From and To, then Review batch. Read Included vouchers, Excluded records, counts, debit/credit totals and Movement by target ledger · INR. Supported types are Receipt, Payment, Contra and Journal, including supported-source reversals as Journal.

Under Explicit target ledger mappings choose Source ledger, Exact target ledger name and Verified target group, confirm the separate-test-company classification, then Save verified mapping. Resolve every unmapped ledger before XML downloads.

Download masters XML, Download vouchers XML and Download reconciliation JSON for the same reviewed batch fingerprint. If data/mappings change, refresh and download the entire batch again; stale fingerprints are rejected.

In a disposable separate TallyPrime 7.2 test company, retain a backup, check existing ledger names/groups and select the XML import facility for masters first, vouchers second. Do not select your live company. Inspect every import result/error; exact menu labels depend on the target installation.

Compare imported voucher count, source references, trial balance and per-ledger debit/credit movement against reconciliation JSON to the paise. Debits are negative XML amounts with ISDEEMEDPOSITIVE Yes; credits are positive with No. Check both sides of each entry, not just a net total.
Test repeated-import behavior only in that disposable company and record results before planning any real migration. Stable source UUIDs are not a guarantee of Tally duplicate prevention.
articles.result: Export is read-only. Accounts reported a successful TallyPrime 7.2 import with no errors. This is an Accounts-reported result, not an independently witnessed import in this help review. Per-ledger reconciliation and repeat-import behavior remain pending unless separately evidenced.

avoid: Opening balances are deliberately excluded even though native opening vouchers exist. Party/bill-wise, tax, correction-note and source-linked membership records are excluded; review the batch's exact reasons.

articles.title: Solve common form and balance problems
articles.why: Most entry errors come from date locks, account choice or unequal lines.
before: Who: approved association registration applicant, within their association.
Keep the voucher description and exact validation message.
steps: “Debits and credits must balance”: check both totals in the fixed footer; enter one positive side per line and use at least two different accounts.
“Receipt/payment/transfer account rule”: verify the cash/bank side and voucher type using the worked examples.
“Outside the open books”: check the start date and locked-through date. Do not alter the transaction date just to bypass the restriction.
“Record changed”: reload the list before another review action; another request may already have processed it.
“Missing membership journal”: check finance policy enabled, receipt acknowledged, positive amount and cutover date. Use the safe missing-receipt posting action.
“Cannot edit posted voucher”: use a linked reversal and corrected entry, not a database update.

Technical operators can run accounting:check with the association argument for existing ledger integrity checks. This is a read-only diagnostic, not a repair, reset or permission override. Escalate failures without changing posted rows.
